lines.text: In December 1872, sailors spotted a merchant brigantine drifting aimlessly across the Atlantic under full canvas.
Boarding the vessel, rescuers found the ship completely seaworthy, but every single soul had vanished without a trace.
Inside the captain's cabin, personal belongings lay untouched, yet the ship's navigation instruments and single lifeboat were gone.
In the dark hold sat seventeen hundred barrels of raw industrial alcoholâ€”nine of them mysteriously empty.
Did escaping alcohol fumes spark fear of an imminent explosion, forcing the crew into a doomed open lifeboat?
A century and a half later, the fate of her ten passengers remains the sea's greatest unsolved riddle. Subscribe to Beyond History for more.
